main_body: A tall dark-grey rune stone slab with a lighter rounded cap at the top, and a front face carrying cyan rune glyphs
top_band: rows 7-10, grey L=92 #5c5a64, 4 rows, but it is the same width as the body with a straight rectangular band (rounded only at the top corners); row 11 is a dark outline/lip
evidence: Column x=8: outline at row 6, then a 4-row lighter grey band (rows 7-10, L=92), then a dark row 11 and the front face (rows 12-30, L=69). The cap is a straight band no wider than the shaft, with only slightly cut corners, and it is only about 23 L lighter than the shaft. This matches the guide's red 'flat band cap' rather than the green ellipse cap, which is wider than the shaft and clearly lighter. The runes are painted flat on the face. Under rule 12 a straight rectangular band that is no wider than the body fails, so the stone reads as a front elevation with a hat.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 5 distinct colours against 38-40 in the references, and a median of 5 colours per tile against 17-20. Its dark edge pixels are 100% neutral, so the outline is a near-black sticker line, while the references are tinted (1% and 33% neutral). The body is two flat greys, with only a few cyan rune pixels and no grain, speckle or per-stone shading. That is far shallower than the references.
